=
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Alok Kumar Sinha, Adv
 For the Respondent/s : Mr.Ajay (Ga-5)
 Ac to Ga-5
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Satyavrat Verma
Oral Order

1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned AC to GA-5.
2.

Learned counsel for the petitioner that land pertaining to Khata Nos. 13, 50 and 71, Khesra No.
774, 775 and 389 area 9 katha at Mauza- Marar Morkahi, District- Khagaria is raiyati land of the petitioner.

3. It is submitted that the said raiyati land of the petitioner has been acquired by the Rural Works Department without any public notice in complete breach of the Land Acquisition Act 2013 for constructing Murkhai Ucch Vidyalaya to Simraha Village Road.

4. It is next submitted that the instant writ petition has been filed seeking compensation of 9 katha of land of the petitioner utilized for constructing the said road without Patna High Court CWJC No.5138 of 2022(3) dt.09-12-2024 acquisition and also to calculate the compensation of 6 katha of land which became useless for the purposes of agriculture in view of the road constructed.

5. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that a counter-affidavit on behalf of Respondent Nos. 2, 5 and 6 dated 1-8-2022 has been filed wherein it has been pleaded that over 9 katha of land, road was constructed by the Panchayat with oil and brick soiling in the Jhaksi Devi @ Jhakho Devi, vs The State Of Bihar, on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192681834/
1 financial year 2015-16 and after three years of the construction of the road by the Panchayat, the up gradation of the road was done by the department under Mukhya Mantri Gramin Sadak Yojana scheme which was completed in the year 2019, further the petitioner at the time of construction of the road never raised any objection, hence is not entitled for compensation in terms of the order dated 25-4-2019 in CWJC No. 8660 of 2019 (Jangli Pandit & Ors. vs. the State of Bihar).
6.

sentences.text:
The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that a reply to the counter-affidavit filed on behalf of Respondent Nos. 2, 5 and 6 has been filed by the petitioner and the petitioner has rebutted the said stand of the respondents, on the ground that this Court while deciding CWJC No. 8660 of 2019, took into consideration the fact that the road Patna High Court CWJC No.5138 of 2022(3) dt.09-12-2024 was constructed under Mukhya Mantri Gramin Sadak Yojana in the year 2008-09 and the scheme under Mukhya Manti Gramin Sadak Yojna for construction of village road did not contemplate acquisition of land, rather consent of the land owner was needed to implement the scheme, further the petitioner while the road was being constructed did not raise any objection for more than 10 years, as such, writ petition was dismissed,
but in the present case, the construction of the road was completed in the year 2019 and the petitioner since before being an illiterate lady was raising objection, as would manifest from letter dated 26-12- 2015 (Annexure R/1 to the Rejoinder) issued by the A.D.M addressed to the C.O to send report regarding measurement of land of the petitioner within 15 days, in view of the letter of the petitioner.
It is submitted that when Panchayat was constructing the road by oil and brick soiling in the year 2015, it was since then the petitioner was objecting.

7. It is next submitted that the petitioners of CWJC No. 8660 of 2019 had prayed for removing the constructed road over their raiyati land after 10 years, while petitioner is claiming compensation,
when it is not in dispute that the land is her raiyati land and the same was used for constructing the aforesaid road without seeking her consent and she had also objected.

It is Patna High Court CWJC No.5138 of 2022(3) dt.09-12-2024 next submitted that petitioner had four sons, but three of them died, as such, petitioner was suffering from mental agony also when her land was utilized for the aforesaid purpose.

8. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State submits that the stand of the State stands pleaded in the counter-affidavit filed on behalf of the Respondent Nos. 2, 5 and 6, but then is not in a position to rebut the submission of the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner that letter dated 26-12-2015 was issued by the A.D.M addressed to the C.O to send a report regarding measurement of the land of the petitioner within 15 days in view of the letter of the petitioner, as she had objected that her raiyati land was being used for the purposes of constructing a soiling road by the Panchayat.

The learned State counsel is also not in a position to rebut the submission of the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner that the consent of the petitioner was not obtained prior to the road being upgraded as being pleaded by the State.

9. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, it becomes clear that it is not the case of the State that the land in question is not the raiyati land of the petitioner, further the counter affidavit does not even remotely suggest that consent of the petitioner was obtained prior to utilizing the raiyati land of Patna High Court CWJC No.5138 of 2022(3) dt.09-12-2024 the petitioner for Jhaksi Devi @ Jhakho Devi, vs The State Of Bihar, on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192681834/
2

sentences.text:
upgrading the aforesaid road, further the reliance of the State on an order of this court in CWJC No.
8660 of 2019 is misplaced for the reason that in the said case the petitioners had approached this Court with a prayer for removing the road from their raiyati land after 10 years of its construction,
which did not persuade the Court to interfere, but in the instant case the petitioner being an illiterate lady and had also suffered mental agony on account of the death of her three sons, but still she had moved before the A.D.M seeking measurement of her land based on which the A.D.M in the year 2015 itself had directed the Circle Officer to submit the measurement report of the land in question, but then it appears that nothing was done.
10.

The Court further fails to appreciate the conduct of the Respondent Nos. 2, 5 and 6 that in their counter affidavit they have very conveniently not produced the letter dated 26- 12-2015 issued by the A.D.M addressed to the C.O, though the C.O is also a party in the instant writ proceedings,
impleaded as Respondent No. 7.
11.

It manifests that the authorities, without seeking consent of the petitioner or even without compensating her, utilised 9 katha of her land for the aforesaid road without Patna High Court CWJC No.5138 of 2022(3) dt.09-12-2024 acquiring the same and giving compensation.
12. At this stage, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State seeks two weeks further time for filing a supplementary counter-affidavit.

13. The Court is not inclined to grant time to the State for filing a supplementary counter-affidavit,
but then directs the District Magistrate and the Circle Officer to file their separate counter-affidavits duly sworn by them.
14.
Put up this case on 17-12-2024, within top five cases under the same heading.
15. In view of the pleading made in the I.A. No. 1 of 2022, the same is allowed.
16. The office is directed to amend the party position, in view of the pleading made in I.A No. 1 of 2022.

(Satyavrat Verma, J) SUMIT/-
